mcat_description.short: Modular tensile structures are pre-engineered, prefabricated outdoor shade and shelter systems comprising a tensioned fabric membrane (typically PVC-coated polyester) stretched over a steel or aluminium frame, sold as modular units or custom-sized installations quoted per square foot.
mcat_description.long: A modular tensile structure is a lightweight, pre-engineered architectural shelter system in which a high-strength fabric membrane — most commonly PVC-coated polyester, PVDF-coated fabric, or PTFE/FRP — is held under tension over a mild steel, galvanised steel, or aluminium structural frame to create weather-resistant, UV-protective outdoor canopies, sheds, and roofing. The 'modular' designation distinguishes these from bespoke large-span tensile membrane architecture: modular units are factory-fabricated in repeatable configurations (conical, hyperbolic, barrel vault, umbrella, tunnel, sail) and assembled on-site with pole-fitted or bolted connections, enabling faster installation and easier disassembly. In the Indian market, these structures are widely used for car parking shades, walkway covers, terrace covers, entrance canopies, food courts, swimming pool enclosures, and industrial/commercial shade applications, with PVC-coated polyester fabric in the 500–900 GSM range being the dominant commercial form. Motorised/retractable variants and German hanger-style large-span modular canopies represent growing sub-segments within this MCAT.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'modular tensile structure' refers to a pre-engineered, factory-fabricated outdoor shelter system where a tensioned fabric membrane is stretched over a mild steel or aluminium frame — distinguished from bespoke large-span tensile architecture by its modular, repeatable unit configuration and on-site assembly. PVC-coated polyester fabric is the dominant material, accounting for the majority of commercial installations due to its balance of cost, weather resistance, and availability; PVDF-coated fabric is used for premium and longer-lifespan applications, while PTFE-coated fibreglass and FRP are used for permanent or high-specification structures. The Indian market is served by a large base of manufacturers concentrated in Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Chennai, Pune, and Bengaluru, with most sellers offering design, fabrication, and installation as a bundled service. Fabric weight (GSM) is a key quality differentiator — common grades range from 500 GSM (light-duty) to 900 GSM (heavy-duty/industrial). The 'German hanger structure' is a recognised trade term in the Indian market for a large-span modular tensile canopy used for commercial and industrial shade, surfacing as a high-impression Google keyword. Motorised and retractable tensile structures are a growing sub-segment, referenced in buyer call data as 'khulne-band hone wala shed.' No specific BIS/IS standard exclusively governs modular tensile structures as a product category; structural design typically references IS 875 (wind loads), IS 1893 (seismic loads), and IS 800 (steel structures), while fabric testing references IS 1969 (tensile properties of fabrics) and IS 12649 (treated/coated fabrics). Lifespan of PVC-coated polyester structures is typically cited as 10–20 years; PTFE-coated fibreglass structures can exceed 30 years.
